audit.whatIsWrong: The page called this FAVOURED at 4/10 while LeBlanc wins only 47.58% of 2150 games.
audit.why: A sub-50% matchup is not favoured. The packet itself flags the contradiction. Difficulty and carry threat moved to EVEN 5.5/10 and 6/10, and the prose that states them was moved with it.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, diffRating 5.5/10, carryRating 6/10, tone amber, breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t restated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike prose leaned on 'Crimson Pact scaling' without the actual conversion, and named LeBlanc's Q 'Chaos Orb'.
audit.why: Crimson Pact is exact: 30 bonus Health gives 1 AP, and 1 AP gives 1.6 bonus Health. Every health item he buys is also damage — that is the real late spike. Riot's Q text calls it a sigil, not a Chaos Orb.
audit.corrected: Spike and Don't text now quote the 30-Health-to-1-AP conversion; the fabricated Q name is gone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two decisive interactions were never stated: untargetability eating your commit, and his sustain requiring Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s and grants 2 seconds untargetable — it does not just dodge damage, it drops your Sigil mark's payoff and any pending Ethereal Chains root. Transfusion costs 0 mana and reaches 4.6s at rank 5, and Hemoplague (120s flat) heals him per champion hit; both are heals, so anti-heal timing decides every extended trade.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries 28s/16s, 4.6s and 120s plus the anti-heal instruction; spikes[2] names Oblivion Orb.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: The 28s rank-1 pool is the single most punishable cooldown in the lane and it halves to 16s by rank 5 — the advice is worthless without the number.

edits.before: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Vladimir carry threat 5/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Vladimir carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Vladimir carry threat 5/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Vladimir carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: Late LeBlanc picks: W the flank, chain the carry, mimic the exit — and vanish before the obituary prints.
edits.after: His health items are AP now and Hemoplague heals per champion hit — pick him alone or do not pick him at all.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Distortion (return) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool (W): 28s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — 2 seconds untargetable that eats a whole combo. Bait it, then commit. - Transfusion costs no mana and hits 4.6s late: chip funds him. - Hemoplague is 120s flat; anti-heal before he casts.

edits.before: Q the sigil, W the detonation, return before the answer — a half-bar round trip he experienced as weather.
edits.after: At 6, Mimic your chain or Distortion — a second entry after his 2-second pool expires is what actually kills him.

edits.before: Vladimir spends Sanguine Pool early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Pool is 28s at rank 1 — plates and roams happen inside that window, before it drops to 16s.

edits.before: Staying at the W landing spot for one more auto — the return timer is your champion; outliving it is optional.
edits.after: Every 30 bonus Health becomes 1 AP for him — while you coast his items compound and your burst stops one-shotting.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling through your combo, healing it back with free Transfusions, and turning health items into AP.

edits.before: Carry through picks — one chained carry per objective; your job is the flank angle and the discipline to leave after.
edits.after: Carry through picks — chain him the instant his pool is spent; 2 seconds of untargetable is the only answer he owns.

edits.before: If Vladimir gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Sanguine Pool extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with W clears and stay relevant through chain picks.
edits.after: If Vladimir gets a kill, Crimson Pact turns that gold into both health and AP — buy Oblivion Orb early and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling, W-clear, and take picks only while his pool is down.

edits.before: Your Chaos Orb burst threatens to kill him before Hemoplague amplifies his team's damage, but Sanguine Pool timing lets him sidestep your all-in if he holds it.
edits.after: Your sigil burst threatens to kill him before Hemoplague amplifies his team's damage, but a held Sanguine Pool sidesteps the all-in — force it, count 28s, then go.

edits.before: Shadowflame lets you burst him down before his Crimson Pact bonus AP from health items starts making his sustained damage scarier in extended trades.
edits.after: Shadowflame plus an early Oblivion Orb matters here — without Grievous Wounds his no-cost Transfusion heals back most of what your first-item burst takes off.

edits.before: Vlad's Crimson Pact scaling off health and AP items combined with Hemoplague team-wide execute threat starts winning extended fights and skirmishes as he out-scales your single burst window.
edits.after: Crimson Pact converts every 30 bonus Health into 1 AP, so his health items are damage too, and Hemoplague's 120s amp plus per-champion heal wins the extended fights your single burst window cannot reach.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 remain in your favor because Distortion lets you re-engage after he pools, effectively negating his one true escape if you're patient enough to bait it twice. Watch for Hemoplague at 6 — if he lands it on you and your team, his sustained damage output starts adding up fast, so try to burst him before that timer starts ticking.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 remain in your favor because Distortion's 4-second return outlasts his 2-second pool: enter, let him submerge, and be there when he surfaces with 28 seconds of nothing. Hemoplague is 120s and heals him for every champion it hits, so never let him cast it into your whole side — chain him first, or fight after it expires.

edits.before: Stack Crimson Pact health/AP items for sustained scaling
edits.after: Buy health items that Crimson Pact converts into AP

notes: CHART: one cross-layer disagreement fixed — phases[6].side read 'Skill' while win[6] and packet.levelChart both read 'Vladimir'; the side is moved onto them and phases[6].why rewritten in the same proposal so the row and its sentence agree. Rows 0-5 already agreed on both layers. SEPARATELY FLAGGED: the packet's own defect list says the chart gives LeBlanc 6 of 7 stages while she wins 47.58%. The kit does not settle which stage is actually wrong — Vladimir's early is weak (no dash, health-cost E) so LeBlanc genuinely does own levels 1-5, but six stages against a losing win rate cannot all be right. Rather than move a row I cannot ground, I moved diff/diffRating/carryRating to match the win rate and left every phases[N].side and win[N] untouched, so the two layers still agree. LeBlanc's Q was called 'Chaos Orb' in spikes[1]; Riot's text only says 'projects a sigil', so I used 'sigil' rather than assert a name the kit file does not carry. Both COPY_PASTE_BLEED lints and the COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT lint are fixed.
